rationale: Read the retained receipt of experiment 3b98f3a057a749ed8b4f4ba2f23f9db7 (CheckRun e1f5bf19d9fa482380acf68d58ec197e, exit 0, 33 events). Its event 32 records a commit-tracking store that also reports itself as monotonic holding a configuration entry at index 1 and ten commands with the commit index staged at 11, and the node constructed from it coming back with an empty configuration while its applied index is 11. The gap therefore does not depend on the store shape, so the parent account's store-breadth limitation is narrowed to production stores; no other claim changes.

interpretations.joint_history: Five receipts of the same harness file answer this question. Two state the gap in clusters (5e1ce9aa430842d5a9325cfecbc885f6 and e1ee764584564a95b3e288381dfb75d9, each at its own indices 0 and 1), one states the gap for a hand-built history in a commit-tracking store that is also monotonic (e1f5bf19d9fa482380acf68d58ec197e at index 32), and two state the repair paths (183f75213c5a4f26a951f76784b3e54f at 15 and 16 for an arriving configuration entry, 5627b36f50384d14851e4b5da991fa96 at 30 and 31 for an installed snapshot).
interpretations.rationale: Current account: with RestoreCommittedLogs enabled a restarted node does not load the committed configuration entries at or below the commit index it recovers; the mechanism is store-independent, both repair paths are measured, and the gap is now reproduced for a second store shape. Mechanism: restoreFromCommittedLogs clamps the store's commit index, applies the recovered range through processLogs (which ends with setLastApplied), and the scan then starts at max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, so a configuration entry at or below that index never reaches processConfigurationLogEntry. Evidence: 5e1ce9aa430842d5a9325cfecbc885f6 and e1ee764584564a95b3e288381dfb75d9 state both shapes in clusters (no snapshot: empty configuration while the log records the voter; snapshot: the snapshot's configuration while the logged change is missing); e1f5bf19d9fa482380acf68d58ec197e states the same outcome for a history written directly into a commit-tracking store that also reports monotonic, with the applied index at the staged commit index of eleven and an empty recovered configuration; 183f75213c5a4f26a951f76784b3e54f shows repair by an arriving configuration entry; 5627b36f50384d14851e4b5da991fa96 shows repair by an installed snapshot with the node's snapshot index jumping while its log index stayed at its pre-shutdown value. Consequences that remain source-derived rather than measured: runFollower refuses to campaign with no known peers, and quorumSize over an empty or stale voter list is wrong; the child questions measure what such a configuration admits, rejects and commits.
counterevidence: Both repair paths are measured: an arriving configuration entry restores the full set while the node is still a member, and an installed snapshot restores it when log replication is impossible, so a cluster with membership traffic, snapshots or a lagging node closes the gap without operator action.
Snapshot configuration is loaded correctly by restoreSnapshot, so the gap needs a committed configuration entry between the last snapshot (or index 0) and the recovered commit index.
The gap reproduces for a commit-tracking store that is also marked monotonic, so it is not an artefact of the store's indexing shape.
No captured test asserts configuration state after a RestoreCommittedLogs restart, so the captured suite neither contradicts nor covers this path.
limitations: Applies to nodes configured with RestoreCommittedLogs=true and a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; with the flag off, lastApplied equals the snapshot index and the scan range is unchanged.
All measurements use in-memory stores (including a hand-built monotonic commit-tracking store) with the repository's in-memory transport and mock FSM; production stores are not measured.

The installed-snapshot repair needed the leader's log to have been compacted past the node's last index, which the probe arranged by letting the cluster commit eighty entries while the node was down; other ways of reaching that state are not measured.
